title: Recording big bands by grouping and moving players
summary: Dooky Chase's 17-piece band and Dave Bartholomew's big band; with few channels he grouped reeds and had players step back or take hand signals to balance.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Can you imagine? Now, that's a name you don't hear.
Yeah. You know, come to think of it. And Dave's big band.

Sure, that's right. You had to do all those sides like with Dave Bartholomew with the big band. Yeah. So when you only had four, how would you do, how would you do, if you had only four, how would you do a big band?

Oh, again, you have to group people. For instance, group reads, say, say if you had two reads or three, you'd group them and then move them physically to balance them level-wise. Right. In other words, if you had two tenors, one guy was just louder than the other, you'd have them moving back a little bit. Right. And listen to you.
Just physically say, hey, step back two. Yeah.
So you blend with the alto better. Right. You know, just because of the nature.
Just because of the nature of the instrument. Yeah.
Yeah. And to the point that sometimes you were trying to give them hand signals to back off a little bit or come up a little bit or whatever, you know?
But that was in the early days. And, and, and, and. You had to use your ingenuity. Yeah. I didn't know. I didn't know what the audience was. I still didn't appreciate who the audience were.
